messages.author: 673086e375eccf25
messages.subject: Binomial regression with genotype data
parts:
Hi to all,

I would like to set up a model where I try to calculate the odds ratio for HLA genotypes. Problem hereby is, that there is a huge number of different HLA alleles - while patient numbers are comparably low - which make calculations very difficult.

Normally I set up a logit regression as follows:

having two alleles A and B, a codominant model would look as follows
 
  logit(Disease probability) = Intercept + number of B alleles * log OR(B)

with more alleles A, B, C, D, E, ...:

  logit(Disease probability) = Intercept + number of B alleles * log OR(B) + number of C alleles * log OR(C) + ..... 

When the number of alleles increases, a hierarchical model with R-INLA would be nicer. However, I would have to reformulate the model somehow

  logit(Disease probability) = Intercept + f( first allele, model="iid") + f( second allele, model = "iid")

The first and the second iid model however should be exactly the same here, because of exchangeability of the first and the second allele.
Moreover, I could try to use relationships between alleles, like genetic distance, and consider it as "spatial" distance. But the iid model might already
be very good to identify possibly interesting HLA alleles as risk alleles.

How can I set up such a model? The "copy" tool might not work here.

Best regards,
Andreas

messages.author: 673086e375eccf25
messages.subject: Re: Binomial regression with genotype data
parts:
... it's not easy to understand. Maybe this reformulation would help:

the basic model is a logit regression, with the assumption of a co-dominant effect of each allele. I.e.:
logit(Disease probability) = Intercept + number of B alleles * log OR(B) + number of C alleles * log OR(C) + ....

= Intercept + B * a_1 + C * a_2 + D * a_3 + ....

Now I would like to introduce a restriction, that all coefficients a_1, ... , a_n come from a common distribution with a_i ~ N( a_mean, a_sd^2).

This resembles somehow the iid model of R-INLA, but I wonder how to express that correctly to make R-INLA calculate this. The input data would look like this, then (example):

Disease    Ntrials   A      B    C   D ....
yes           3          1       1    0    0                      for  AB genotype  (== BA genotype!!!)
no            2           2       0    0    0                     for AA genotype
yes           2          0       1    1    0                     for BC genotype
etc.

I would like to have an odds ratio for disease risk for each allele. And I believe that all odds ratios come from a normal distribution.

The more complicated idea is to include phylogenetic information, i.e. a tree of genetic distances between  different alleles.

Best regards,
Andreas

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: Binomial regression with genotype data
parts:
Hi

as Ryan suggested, there is a undocumented model called 'z'. this has
been around for quite a long time, but its internal implementation is
based on a 'hack' (and is hard to maintain) and therefore I want to
remove it and replace it with something more appropriate. morover, the
'z' model do

linear.predictor = ..... + Z %*% z

where z ~ N(0, prec * I), and Z is a fixed matrix, and the prior for
(log)prec is hyper=list(prec = list(prior=..,param=...)))

the model is internally expanded into 'm' submodels, so you'll get
results like this

r$summary.random$idx.1$mean

for the first element of 'z', and .2 for the second etc.


looking at the joint distribution for

(Z %*% z, z)

we can rewrite this as a 'generic' model. this is the idea in some new
code, which is a wrapper to existing models,

new.z.model = inla.model.wrapper(covariates = Z, model="joint",
Q = diag(m))

r = inla(y ~ 1 + f(idx, model=new.z.model),
data = list(y=y, idx=idx))


and then you'll get the posterior for (Z %*% z, z), so what you're after
is here:

r$summary.random$idx[(n+1):(n+m),"mean"]


as the last 'm' elements of that vector. this model is more general as
'z' can have any prior precision matrix. the prior for its scaling, can
be set with hyper = list(prec = list(...))) as before

it might be we can do the 'wrapper'-call internally in the f-function,
so it will be hided from the user

to conclude: there is an approach on its way out, and a new better one
on its way in, but neither ones are stable. the new one is 'in progress'
and needs more work. I'll put this on the todo-list.

OOPS: in the future then model 'z' will go away and the new 'wrapper'
one will be changed (or even appear as something else, as we're not
convinced about the general usefulness of the 'wrapper'-based models),
but I'll post it here when its done.



*******************

EXAMPLE:

z = rnorm(m)
Z = matrix(rnorm(m*n), n, m)
y = 1 + Z %*% z
idx = 1:n

r = inla(y ~ 1 + f(idx, model='z', Z = Z),
data = list(y=y, idx=idx, Z=Z))


new.z.model = inla.model.wrapper(covariates = Z, model="joint", Q =
diag(m))
r = inla(y ~ 1 + f(idx, model=new.z.model),
data = list(y=y, idx=idx))




new.z.model = inla.model.wrapper(covariates = Z, model="joint", Q =
diag(m))
r = inla(y ~ 1 + f(idx, model=new.z.model),
data = list(y=y, idx=idx))

print(r$summary.random$idx[(n+1):(n+m),"mean"] - z)



******************************

Hi,

I tried the "z" model ... however, it did not work out with a binomial response.

This is just one example of different trials:

fit2 <- inla(I(Group=="Case") ~ 1 + f(ID, model="z", Z=hlaMatrix),
  data=list(ID=1:nrow(hla), Group=hla$Group, Ntrials=rep(1,nrow(hla2)), hlaMatrix = hla2), Ntrials=Ntrials, family="binomial")

Error in inla(Group ~ 1 + f(ID, model = "z", Z = hlaMatrix), data = list(ID = 1:nrow(hla),  :
  The response for family[1] is not of type 'numeric|list|matrix'; don't know what to do.

ID is here just a row number
Group the binomial variable "Case" or "Control"
Ntrials was set here to "1" for each individual row. I also used "aggregate" to use the Ntrials variable correctly.
hla2 is the covariance matrix of genotype data - as described

Does this mean that the "z" model does not work with a binomial link function?

Best regards,
Andreas

the problem is that

I(Group == "Case")

returns an object of class 'AsIs'.

try to do

y = as.numeric(I(Group == "Case"))

and then use 'y' as the response.
